title: One repository whose dependencies live in Maven, NuGet, crates.io, and the Go proxy
why: Until these manifests were parsed a Java, .NET, Rust, or Go service scanned as a repository that depends on nothing — indistinguishable, in every downstream surface, from one that genuinely has no dependencies. This case pins the four parsers and the three places they must not guess: an unresolvable Maven property, a Cargo path dependency, and a Go module a replace directive redirects.

facts.note: the version comes from the pom's own property, resolved rather than left as ${spring.version}
test scope is still a declared dependency
Version as a child element, not an attribute
the lockfile resolves the caret range the manifest declares
a replace directive redirects the build, so the declared version is not the resolved one
the property that names its version is defined in a parent pom the scanner never fetched

absent_facts.note: a path dependency is not a crates.io package, and cataloguing it would offer upgrade targets for a crate that was never published
an unresolved version must leave the dependency versionless rather than inventing one
the replaced module keeps no resolved version
